findings.title: The `[codex]` install hint is swallowed by Rich markup
findings.description:
The central value is "the exact command to fix it" (lines 28, 171, 190, 211). The command contains `[codex]`.
- `doctor.py:78` prints `console.print(f"    [dim]fix: {row.fix_hint}[/dim]")`.
- `models.py:112` passes cell strings to `table.add_row`, and `auth.py` uses `rprint`.
- Rich parses `[codex]` as a style tag and drops it, so the user sees `pip install 'squadron-ai'` or `(needs  extra)`.
- The design says the hint is defined once but never says how it is escaped (`rich.markup.escape`) or printed raw. The marker `(needs [codex] extra)` at line 173 has the same problem.

findings.title: Missing-extra error order, and a wrong claim about `get_provider`
findings.description:
- Line 76 says the provider registers "so `get_provider("openai-oauth")` can raise the install hint rather than 'unknown provider'". `registry.get_provider` only raises `KeyError` for unregistered names (`registry.py:22-24`), and the hint is raised at `create_agent`. The provider already imports cleanly today, because `agent.py` imports the SDK lazily.
- `CodexProvider.create_agent` (`provider.py:32-34`) checks `strategy.is_valid()` first and raises `ProviderAuthError("No Codex credentials…")`.
- The design never says where `resolve_codex_runtime()` goes relative to that check. If it keeps the current order, a user with no extra and no login gets the credentials error, not the install hint.
- That contradicts the success criterion at line 190 ("any `openai-oauth` use exits with an error containing the exact install command") and walkthrough step 1 (lines 209-210), which is a fresh install with no login.

findings.title: Missing-extra and hang behavior is undefined for login, logout and status
findings.description:
The Failure Modes table covers only the Codex turn.
- **Missing extra:** `sq auth login/logout/status openai-oauth` without `openai_codex` is not covered. The status row (line 126) names only "timeout or SDK error", not `ImportError`. `tests/cli/test_auth.py:66` (`test_auth_status_valid_and_missing`) sets `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so `openai-oauth` is valid through the key fallback. Status would then call `account_summary()` with the extra absent, which the Integration Requirements (line 204) say must pass. A user who has `auth.json` but removed the extra also cannot log out.
- **Unbounded startup hangs:** `codex.turn_timeout_s` wraps only `thread.run` (line 125), and `login_timeout_s` bounds only `handle.wait()` (line 108). A hang in `AsyncCodex.__aenter__`/`initialize` or `thread_start` during a turn is unbounded. So is runtime start in login. `logout()` has no timeout or failure row at all.
- **Timeout leaves the thread live:** line 128 says "turn handle interrupted", but the data flow uses `thread.run`, which exposes no handle. The timeout row does not clear `_codex`/`_thread`, unlike the transport-closed row (line 129). A recovery turn on the same agent would then land on a thread whose turn is still running.

findings.title: Existing codex tests the design breaks are not enumerated
findings.description:
Line 199 says tests are faked "as existing codex tests do" but never lists what changes. The following existing tests fail under the design:
- `tests/providers/codex/test_agent.py` mocks `codex_app_server` and `codex_app_server.client`, and patches `agent.resolve_codex_binary`.
- `test_none_response_yields_empty` (line 168) asserts that a `None` response yields `""`, which D8 forbids.
- `_MockRunResult` has no `status`, so every happy-path test fails the D8 status check.
- `test_effort_logs_one_warning` asserts the WARNING that D5 removes.
- `test_subsequent_message_reuses_thread` uses `assert_awaited_once_with("follow up")`, which breaks once `effort=` is passed.
- `test_sdk_import_error_raises` matches `"not installed"`.
- `tests/providers/codex/test_provider.py` patches `agent.resolve_codex_binary` in four places and matches `"npm i -g @openai/codex"`. The `validate_credentials` tests rely on `codex_app_server` importability.
The design should say these are rewritten, not left to be discovered as failures.

findings.title: pyright "clean" ignores the existing exclusion and `reportMissingImports`
findings.description:
`pyproject.toml:95` excludes `providers/codex/agent.py` from strict mode (tech-debt F050). `reportMissingImports = true` (line 98) is set, and the dev group has no `openai-codex`.
- The new `login.py` and `runtime.py` would be strict-checked and report unresolved `openai_codex` imports in the default dev environment.
- The design does not say whether to add the extra to the dev group, add per-import ignores, or keep or drop the `agent.py` exclusion. The old `# pyright: ignore` comments in `agent.py` also go away or move.
- "pyright clean" at line 201 is not achievable as specified.

findings.title: `sq model list` surface does not match the code
findings.description:
- The command is `sq models` / `sq models list` (`app.py:55`). The design says `sq model list` throughout, including the walkthrough.
- There is no "Notes/Profile cell" in default output. The Notes column exists only in verbose mode and is truncated to 30 characters (`models.py:136`). Line 173 requires the marker "in default and verbose output" but does not say which cell holds it. A 30-character cut would clip the `(needs … extra)` text.
- Resolving "each alias's profile through `ensure_provider_loaded` + `get_provider`" needs `get_profile(alias["profile"]).provider` first. User aliases can name an unknown profile (`_profile_rank` handles that case explicitly). `ensure_provider_loaded` swallows `ImportError`, and `get_provider` raises `KeyError`. The design gives no handling, and today `models list` never resolves profiles, so it cannot currently fail this way.

findings.title: The doctor row has an unsupplied data source, and the `codex CLI` row is wrongly called unrelated
findings.description:
- D9 says the row's "package version, runtime source" come from `CodexRuntime`, but `CodexRuntime` is `(source, path|None)` (line 63). Neither the package version nor the login state is available. Doctor would need `importlib.metadata`, which D9 forbids it from doing. "Login state from auth.json presence" has no accessor: `OAuthFileStrategy._auth_file` is private, and `is_valid()` also returns True for `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Line 172 says the existing `codex CLI` row is "unrelated to the SDK". But `setup_steps.py:139` describes it as enabling "the codex provider", and `sq setup` offers "Install Codex CLI" (`npm i -g`). After this slice a bundled-binary user permanently sees a WARN and an npm install step that contradicts "no npm". The row's text and gating role should be addressed.

findings.title: The `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback is left as an implementation fork, and related surfaces stay stale
findings.description:
The design says the fallback is "resolved in this slice", but it only defers a run-and-see check to task 0, and the status, hint and tests depend on the result.
- `setup_hint` ("Run 'codex' CLI to authenticate…", `auth.py:64`) is changed only in the "fails" branch. In both outcomes it should now point to `sq auth login openai-oauth`, since `create_agent` and `sq auth login` display it.
- `status`/`login` call `account()` for a profile that is valid via the key only. That call returns no ChatGPT account, but the design assumes `account.root` is `ChatgptAccount` (line 54). That case has no handling.
- Walkthrough step 8 (line 219) expects `✗ not authenticated` after logout. That is true only when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset. Step 6 uses `env -u` for exactly that reason, which suggests the key is set in the walkthrough environment.

findings.title: D8 bypasses the existing empty-turn recovery, and error types ignore the established hierarchy
findings.description:
- `review_client._collect_review` (`review_client.py:372`) recovers from an empty turn only when the provider raises `EmptyFinalTurnError`, with one retry via `FINISH_REVIEW_PROMPT`. D8 raises plain `ProviderError("Codex turn completed with no response text")`, so a Codex empty turn becomes a hard failure with no recovery. The design never mentions this convention. If Codex deliberately opts out, the design should say so.
- Line 114 also cites issue #15 (the dispatch no-op bug) as justification. Failing `failed`/`interrupted`/empty turns is a behavior change to the existing path that goes beyond the plan entry.
- `errors.py` already defines `ProviderTimeoutError`, `ProviderRateLimitError` ("a long unattended campaign should pause on this") and `ProviderAuthError`. The table maps timeout, `ServerBusyError`/`RetryLimitExceededError` and not-logged-in (lines 125, 130, 131) to plain `ProviderError`. Callers that discriminate on subclass lose the signal.
- `ProviderError` carries `telemetry`/`duration_seconds` so failure artifacts record cost (slice 931 D12). The failed and interrupted rows do not attach the `usage` they might have.

findings.title: Token-usage stamping is under-specified against how the review pipeline consumes it
findings.description:
D6 says to stamp "the same metadata keys the OpenAI agent uses" (`usage`, `turns`).
- `turn_capture.collect_turn` reads `metadata["turns"]` and sums it as "requests sent". The design never says what Codex stamps there: `1` per `thread.run`, or omitted. `1` would misreport the number of model requests.
- The OpenAI agent stamps a `TokenUsage` object whose fields may be `None`, not a `None` `usage`. Line 134 says "`TokenUsage` left `None`", but the capture type is `TokenUsage`, not `TokenUsage | None`. The design should say "no `usage` key" or "an all-`None` `TokenUsage`", and which fields are stamped.
- `review/models.py:233,245` and `review_client.py:258,310` comment that Codex "never stamps" or "cannot apply" values. Those statements become stale and need updating.

findings.title: Login behavior under the real CLI shape is unspecified
findings.description:
- `auth_login` and `auth_status` are synchronous Typer commands (`auth.py:19,40`), while `InteractiveLogin` methods are `async`. The design does not say how they are bridged. `status` would need one `asyncio.run` and runtime spawn per valid interactive profile.
- What `sq auth login openai-oauth` does when the profile is already valid is unspecified: re-run the browser flow or print the current state. Today's login on a valid profile is non-interactive.
- `--timeout SECONDS` is passed as `float`, but config keys are typed `int` (`cf.mcp_timeout_s`, `keys.py:356-359`).
- Exit codes are not stated for success, `success=False`, and the unsupported-profile errors. Today's failed validation exits 0 (`test_auth_login_missing_key`). The design says "non-zero" only for timeout (line 127).

findings.title: Proportionality: mechanisms and prose a single consumer does not need
findings.description:
Candidates to cut or defer:
- Two new runtime-checkable Protocols (`InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement`) plus a typed `CodexRuntime`. Each has exactly one implementer and one or two callers. The "Provides to Other Slices" section (lines 178-181) lists them although the frontmatter admits no slice consumes them. D3 and D9 can stay for the no-string-dispatch rule, but the "provides" claims should go.
- `codex.account_timeout_s` and `codex.login_timeout_s` as user-facing config keys, plus a `--timeout` flag that duplicates one of them. A single constant, or one key, would meet the requirement. Only `turn_timeout_s` is clearly a tunable.
- The "Runtime startup cost" paragraph (line 82) is justification prose for a non-requirement, since it says no latency target is set. The "Relationship to the architecture's auth model" section (lines 88-89) is a restatement. The per-row test mandate (line 199) multiplies tests for 12 rows, several of which share one code path.

findings.title: D2 and D5 rest on SDK facts that cannot be verified in this repo
findings.description: `openai_codex` is not installed in the checkout, so the `codex_cli_bin` module name, `ReasoningEffort` members, `TurnStatus`, `TransportClosedError`, `account().root`, and `usage.last` could not be checked. The design's mitigation, a real-types test skipped when the extra is absent (line 200), is only effective if CI installs the extra at least once. That is not stated. The squadron side checks out: `Effort` has `none, low, medium, high, xhigh`.
